races.name: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good and has placed form at the trip; prominent racing style is perfectly suited to tracking Lady Dublin and striking inside the final furlong, and Easterby's yard is in red-hot form at T14 8/68.

runners_data.name: Trust Havana
runners_data.note: Form figures of 6-8-10 are uninspiring and her true style is closing from the rear — she is held up by nature but the crowded hold-up section means she will likely race closer to midfield than ideal, which further blunts her chance.

runners_data.name: Bea Kindly
runners_data.note: 69 days off the track is a significant flag, her best figures have come over 5f, and she has finished ninth twice in three runs on Good ground; naturally a hold-up type who will be squeezed into a midfield role that does not play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Spirit of Mary
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort in her most recent start but is a genuine hold-up horse operating out of position here; Ben Haslam sends her in with a 2/8 T14 strike-rate and she steps back up to 6f where her form reads 3-7, mixed at best.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Best effort was a third over 5f on Good; her natural closing style means she arrives at this 6f trip with a slight question mark, and she will need a strong pace that this map does not guarantee to deliver her late.

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Fahey yard is active (T14 4/40) and she has course-relevant 6f form, but she is a natural closer being funnelled into midfield by the congested hold-up group — her STYLE_FIT flag is a real discount in a race likely run at a controlled tempo.

runners_data.name: Liveadream
runners_data.note: Second over 7f on Good suggests she stays, and Sam James is a capable jockey, but she is a true hold-up performer racing out of position in midfield; the extra furlong she would need to pick off rivals in a sedate pace race may simply not materialise.

runners_data.name: Crystal Kraken
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a placed effort over 6f on Good (3/6f/GOO) and Rossa Ryan takes the ride; sits in an ideal tactical position to track Lady Dublin and represents one of the most style-compatible winners in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, won over this course and distance on Good ground recently and carries a headgear flag; Jake Dickson (7) claims and the biggest risk is she is topped on OR (65) but she dictates all the fractions.

runners_data.name: Eevee Star
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) worn and Bethell's yard is active (T14 5/30); naturally a hold-up horse but sits at the shallower end of the closer group which may allow a slightly more forward berth — 3/6f/GOO last time out is a useful form reference.

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: Jason Hart is a quality booking for Easterby and a placed effort over 6f on Good from three runs back is solid for this grade; closes from hold-up but is not redistributed, so likely to occupy a genuine rear-midfield position and needs more pace than Lady Dublin is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) worn and placed twice in five runs, all on Good or similar; David O'Meara sends her here nine days after her last run and she has consistent placed form at 6f on Good, though her natural hold-up style leaves her reliant on late gaps appearing.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Dublin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner nursery handicap and should stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting what figures to be a controlled, sustainable gallop over Thirsk's straight six furlongs on Good ground. With no rival willing or able to dispute the lead, she can dictate her own fractions and avoid the energy-sapping battles that would expose her stamina reserves, creating a race run at an honest but unfrenetic pace that will not necessarily string the field out early. The large cluster of hold-up horses — Claret And Blues, Liveadream, Trust Havana, Spirit of Mary and Bea Kindly — are genuine closers by nature but are mapped to midfield here precisely because the field cannot accommodate five true hold-up types at the rear; in practice, runners like Liveadream and Claret And Blues are most likely to secure the best midfield berths, while the others may be squeezed wider or further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone leader on a fair pace with a dense midfield pack — strongly favours horses tracking prominently just off the pace, specifically Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken, who can ride the slipstream and pounce without needing a sustained finishing burst from an unpromising position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Dublin Leads, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin bowls along in front unchallenged and the prominent trackers travel smoothly into contention from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Lady Dublin controls pace and fractions, allowing Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken to cruise into her slipstream and deliver their challenges in the final furlong without ever being out of their comfort zone. A controlled tempo on Good ground over 6f at Thirsk suits horses who can race close to the pace and sustain their effort rather than produce a sharp late kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Lady Dublin Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin's fractions are slow enough that she conserves energy and the field cannot close the gap in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace flatters the leader's stamina and leaves the chasing pack with insufficient runway to reel her in, particularly if Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken are unable to quicken sharply off a slow tempo. Lady Dublin, who won over this course and distance on Good ground recently, would prove hardest to peg back under Jake Dickson with a clear advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pick Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front two tire inside the final furlong, allowing genuine midfield types to storm through.
scenarios.body: Eevee Star, Inns And Out and Mardy Bum, who all have recent form at the trip and sit within striking distance, could benefit if Lady Dublin's lead evaporates late and the prominent horses flatten out. This scenario requires a genuinely strong gallop that is not well-supported by this pace map, given Lady Dublin is uncontested, making it the least mechanically likely of the mainstream outcomes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If congestion in the straight creates gaps for the redistributed closers who manage to find a clear run despite their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: Liveadream or Claret And Blues, if able to thread through on Good ground that rewards sustained galloping, could deliver a late flourish, but both are racing out of their natural role in this shape and carry a meaningful style-fit discount. This is a low-probability scenario entirely dependent on pace collapse and a clean passage that this race configuration is unlikely to provide.

watchPoints.text: Lady Dublin's fractions through the first 2f will determine the entire race shape — if she gathers momentum and puts daylight between herself and the field by halfway, Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken must be close enough to pounce or the race is over.

Claret And Blues and Liveadream are natural closers racing out of their preferred position; watch whether they can find a clean passage in the final 2f or whether traffic on Thirsk's straight track costs them any realistic chance.

Lairy Mary steps up to 6f from a run over 5f — she has a win on Good but her form at six furlongs (one run, finishing fourth) is less proven; watch whether she sustains her effort all the way to the line or finds the extra furlong stretching her stamina.

Bea Kindly returns from 69 days off the track and has two runs of 9th on Good ground — if she shows any signs of market support at the off, it would be a significant form reversal worth monitoring, but at face value she looks out of her depth here.

races.name: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Tim Easterby returning 27 days after a modest effort; Good ground suits per his history but the best of his recent form has come at 14f rather than today's 1m6f, and finishing eighth in similar company last time out warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Tupero
runners_data.note: Proven front runner with two recent wins on Good ground, carrying a strong STYLE_FIT tag because the wider field is stacked with hold-up types; wears a hood, handled 14f-15f well and has every chance to dictate an uncontested lead, though his OR of 68 on a 54-day break may catch up with him late.

runners_data.name: Port George
runners_data.note: Hasn't run for 325 days — that layoff is the headline concern — and while his best form shows a second over 12f on Good ground, he is a natural deep closer whose mapped midfield position understates how far back he is likely to race; Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero have only two runners in form over 14 days, limiting confidence in his fitness.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Approach
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has two wins and six placed efforts from ten Good-ground starts, ran just 13 days ago, and his hold-up style suits a race where he can stalk Tupero before producing a late challenge; his OR of 75 is the highest in the field and his best win came over 14f, making today's step up to 1m6f a slight unknown.

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type whose natural closing run is mapped to midfield due to the density of hold-up horses in this small field; showed ability with a third over 16f and 17f on Good ground, but the STYLE_FIT discount applies and his lowest OR in the field (62) reflects limited scope against today's rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Tupero is the sole confirmed front runner in a five-horse field over 1m6f at Thirsk on Good ground, and with no rival willing or able to press him, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The four hold-up types — Gibside, Gaelic Approach, Port George, and Twilight Safari — will settle in behind, though Port George and Twilight Safari are genuine deep closers who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is insufficient front-end supply to place them further back on the map. With Tupero dictating an uncontested rhythm, the race is likely to be run at a measured gallop that rewards a well-timed challenge from mid-to-late in the straight rather than a searching test of stamina. This shape firmly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit close enough to Tupero and pounce in the final two furlongs — genuine hold-up types arriving from the back will need an honest tempo that may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tupero Controls, Sits Tight
scenarios.trigger: If Tupero leads unchallenged and sets a fair but measured pace, forcing hold-up horses to produce their challenge on Tupero's terms.
scenarios.body: Tupero dictates from the front, conserving energy on a Good surface over 1m6f and kicking clear when challenged in the straight; horses who have tracked him closely throughout are best placed to respond. Gaelic Approach, with strong form on Good ground at this trip, and Gibside, an experienced hold-up type, are the likeliest chasers to threaten.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses breaks more prominently than usual and tracks Tupero closely enough to pounce before the deep closers can close.
scenarios.body: A horse that secures a position just off Tupero's shoulder benefits from the lack of genuine pace pressure, making its move two furlongs out before the true hold-up horses can mount their challenge. Gaelic Approach, with two wins on Good ground at 14f and a trainer running in form, fits this profile best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Tupero sets a stronger pace than expected, creating enough of a genuine test of stamina to bring the deepest closers into play.
scenarios.body: Port George and Twilight Safari, both true hold-up types, would relish a more searching gallop that stretches the race out and sees front-runners tie up late, though both carry STYLE_FIT tags and are not naturally positioned for this race shape. The 325-day absence of Port George and Twilight Safari's inconsistent recent form add meaningful doubt to this scenario landing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Compounds
scenarios.trigger: If Tupero is pressured or misjudges the pace and weakens late, allowing the entire field to flow past.
scenarios.body: Without natural pressers in the field this is unlikely, but a gross misjudgement of tempo by Tupero could see Gaelic Approach or Gibside pick up the pieces. Even in this outcome the race would still tend to favour the closest tracker rather than the deepest closer.

watchPoints.text: Tupero's ability to set an uncontested, controlled tempo is the single biggest tactical factor — if he bowls along untroubled, the race shape becomes very difficult for the deepest closers to overcome.
Port George's 325-day absence is a significant fitness question; watch how quickly he warms up in the market and in the preliminaries — a cold price despite the layoff would be telling.
Gaelic Approach is the horse most likely to break cover early and challenge Tupero sooner than expected, which could transform the race into a two-horse duel well before the straight.

With four hold-up horses in a field of five, watch how orderly or chaotic the grouping behind Tupero is — if several fight for position, the horse that settles most smoothly will have a significant energy advantage late.

Twilight Safari and Port George both carry STYLE_FIT tags as redistributed closers; if the pace does not genuinely stretch, monitor whether their jockeys adapt and push forward rather than sitting in a non-existent pocket.

races.name: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who handles Good ground well (10 similar-going runs, 2 wins) but is freshest of all runners at just 2 days since last run — a wide draw or early scrimmage could see her lose her position in a crowded chasing pack; visor reported.

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for John Butler whose T14 rate of 4/10 suggests yard is in form, but her five recent starts are all over 5f on Soft or Stand — stepping up to 6f on Good at Thirsk is an untested combination and she will need pace to run into.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: A genuine deep hold-up type at heart despite appearing on the midfield map, placed in two of three Good-ground starts but requiring others to force the pace; the 6-day turnaround for Micky Hammond is worth noting, and racing off its natural role here tempers its claims.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) and a solid 1 win from 9 similar-going runs suggest she is honest on Good, but Harry Russell navigates a horse who has placed only twice from those nine attempts and whose form string shows a wide range of finishing positions — most likely to be seen in the rear half.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent prominent racer: five of five recent starts on Good going have produced placings (0W7P in similar conditions), and Jason Hart's positive record complements a horse that settles quickly and stays on — ideal profile for a race where the lead is uncontested.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old for Julie Camacho who has placed on her only Good-ground start, handles 6f and likes a prominent pitch; Ryan Sexton keeps it straightforward, and with only 4 runs the scope for improvement is real, though the T14 figure of 1/15 suggests the yard is not peaking right now.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Wears hood and tongue-tie and has been racing exclusively over 7f recently — stepping back to 6f may help Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) get her into a better early position, but the Fahey yard's T14 strike rate of 4/40 is low and she has not placed in any of her last five runs.

runners_data.name: Zooella
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's in-form 3-year-old (T14: 12/43) landed her first win over 6f at Sandown last time and is the sole confirmed front-runner here; Rossa Ryan will look to use the Good ground and an unchallenged lead to dictate fractions and make the race suit her in a field where no one else is likely to push her.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's experienced 6-year-old has a 2-win record on Good ground over 5f and Duran Fentiman rides positively — stepping to 6f is slightly against the grain of her recent form, but the T14 rate of 8/68 is steady and she has the tactical pace to get a good prominent position if the scrimmage resolves quickly.

races.paceDynamic: Zooella is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Rossa Ryan in the saddle for an in-form Ralph Beckett yard, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground at Thirsk — a track where pacemakers who avoid a battle can find a rhythm and be very hard to catch over 6f. Behind her, Miss Rainbow, Taygar, Celtic Arrow and Canaria Queen all want prominent positions, creating a congested group of four chasing the lead and raising the prospect of interference or scrimmaging between the 2f and 3f markers. The hold-up contingent of Love Alive, Eartha and Ziggy's Queen will sit deepest, but at just 9 runners on a flat 6f track the gaps may not materialise quickly enough to allow a sustained late run. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can land a handy position early and control their own fate, rather than closers who will need pace collapse that a lone, unpressured leader is unlikely to provide. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure a comfortable berth — Canaria Queen, with her strong early pace profile and in-form connections, and Taygar, whose consistency from the front rank is proven, are best-placed to actually get their position behind Zooella; Miss Rainbow is most vulnerable to being shuffled wider or back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zooella leads, prominent chase
scenarios.trigger: If Zooella dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent chasers settle cleanly behind her from the outset.
scenarios.body: Zooella controls fractions from the front with minimal pressure, leaving the four prominent pursuers to fight for the best tracking positions — those who secure the rail or a clean passage into the final 2f will finish fastest of all. This shape overwhelmingly suits front-running and prominent profiles who race close to the tempo and can pounce when Zooella is challenged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent scrimmage, pace slows
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types jostle aggressively for position, disrupting rhythm and forcing Zooella to steady behind a wall of horses in the first 2f.
scenarios.body: A fractured early pace creates bunching approaching the 3f pole, compressing the field and setting up a sprint finish from the 2f mark that suits a horse with a sharp finishing kick. Runners who ride prominently but can switch off briefly — Canaria Queen and Celtic Arrow — benefit most from the resulting muddled gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and leave a clear lane for closers to accelerate through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Love Alive and Eartha would need a fast pace and an unimpeded clear run to threaten from off the back — conditions that are unlikely given a single, unforced front-runner. Oasis Cover is a genuine hold-up type shuffled into a midfield map position, but even in this scenario its chances are tempered by the probability it cannot find its true position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Zooella is pressured hard from the start and the entire field quickens prematurely, burning out the prominent group before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An all-out gallop from the off exhausts the early speed horses and hands closers their best opportunity of the day, with Ziggy's Queen and Love Alive — both at their best given time and space — firing late into a depleted field. This scenario depends on something forcing Zooella into a genuine duel, which the current race map does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion alert: Miss Rainbow, Taygar, Celtic Arrow and Canaria Queen all target the same early positions — watch for bumping or checked momentum between the 2f and 3f poles as all four attempt to track Zooella.

Zooella's lead position is uncontested on paper but if Canaria Queen or Miss Rainbow pressures her inside the first furlong, fractions could quicken earlier than expected and compromise her stamina over the final 100 yards.

Oasis Cover's true hold-up style is masked by its midfield map position — punters should not expect it to race forward; if the closers get no run, this horse is most at risk of finishing without ever being seen in the race.

Ziggy's Queen drops back from her recent 7f trips to 6f at Thirsk — monitor whether Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) uses the shorter distance to position her closer than usual, as that would represent a meaningful change in race tactics for this horse.

Love Alive's switch from 5f turf to 6f on Good ground is an unproven combination based on her last five runs — if she fails to settle behind a controlled pace, Alistair Rawlinson will have limited options from the rear of the field.

races.name: JW4x4 Northallerton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with four wins and five places from 15 runs on similar going; proven at 14f on Good and ticks the trip and ground boxes, though needs the pace to be genuine to deploy his finishing effort from off the pace — headgear (hood) may help focus him.|

runners_data.name: Wolf of Badenoch
runners_data.note: Recent course-and-distance winner on Good ground is the standout form angle here; Stevie Donohoe takes over and the horse's one previous win in this field is at 11f on Good, suggesting he appreciates fast conditions and may be well-suited if the gallop stretches the field.|

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner whose style is to lead but whose STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals he is marginally out of his comfort zone here; Ollie Pears has had two winners from six in the last 14 days and this horse's strong Good-ground record (12/15 sim-going) and three wins at 16f+ give him genuine staying credentials to exploit an uncontested lead.|

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Three wins from seven runs at 12f-13f on Good ground give this horse strong form credentials, but as a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear, the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded back-end of this small field rather than his preferred tactics — his chance depends on a strong enough tempo to bring his finishing run into play.|

runners_data.name: Educate
runners_data.note: Career form shows a placed effort on Good at 14f but overall record is modest (0W1P from 15 similar-going runs) and he has not won in his last six; the tongue-tie flag and Micky Hammond's 3/13 recent trainer strike rate provide mild stable interest, yet as a horse whose natural style is hold-up and who is mapped forward by necessity, his chance must be tempered accordingly.|

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 1m4f handicap at Thirsk and, with no rival likely to dispute the lead aggressively, will control tempo from the outset at a sustainable, measured gallop on Good ground. Sixty Plus and Wolf of Badenoch are genuine hold-up types who will settle at the rear and rely on a strong finish, while Dubai Venture and Educate are also natural hold-up horses — their redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the congestion at the rear of this small field, not their actual preferred role. With the tempo set by a single, unchallenged pace-maker at a comfortable clip over this stamina test, the race shape is most likely to favour hold-up horses with a strong late run, provided Max Of Stars does not steal an uncontested advantage that proves impossible to peg back. This is a shape that rewards patience and a sustained gallop home rather than a sharp kick, and horses proven at the distance on Good ground — particularly those with genuine hold-up credentials — hold the tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars bowls along uncontested at a fair-to-slow gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars sets his own fractions with no rival willing to press him, reaches the home straight with a clear advantage and simply stays on to repel any challengers; his strong sim-going record of 12/15 on Good and proven stamina at this trip make him a genuine threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is honest enough to stretch the field and the closers have enough room to deliver sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: With Max Of Stars setting a genuine pace, the rear trio — Sixty Plus and Wolf of Badenoch in particular — get the strong, unrelenting gallop they need to close the gap through the final two furlongs at Thirsk; Wolf of Badenoch's recent win on Good ground and Sixty Plus's consistent placed form at this distance support their claims in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Dubai Venture or Educate secure a better berth than expected and use it to pick off a tiring leader late.
scenarios.body: Dubai Venture has a strong recent record of wins and places at this trip on Good ground and, if the pace is hot enough to tire Max Of Stars, could emerge as a credible finisher from a handy position; Educate's form has been modest but consistency at 12f-14f gives him a residual chance if pace collapse opens the door.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars crawls and the race degenerates into a sprint finish off a false pace.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run affair would theoretically suit anyone with tactical speed, but in a field of genuine middle-distance stayers running out of their natural positions this scenario is highly unlikely to produce a clean result for any single profile; Max Of Stars would still be best placed in front, though Wolf of Badenoch's speed over shorter trips earlier in his career gives him residual interest.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars (Harry Russell) — watch whether he is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged; if no rival applies pressure from the outset, his uncontested lead on Good ground over 1m4f could prove very difficult to reel in.

Wolf of Badenoch — his recent Good-ground win and proven form at the trip make him the most likely closer to threaten, but watch whether Stevie Donohoe can find clear daylight from the rear in a five-runner field where gaps may not materialise quickly.

Dubai Venture — a genuinely strong record at this trip and going profile but watch that Tom Eaves is not caught too far back in his natural hold-up position; in a small, slowly-run field he may struggle to bridge the gap if Max Of Stars steals too big a break.

Sixty Plus (hood) — the headgear change is worth noting for focus and early behaviour; watch his early position under Rossa Ryan as any tendency to race too freely or too far back in a small field could compromise his late run.

Educate (tongue-tie) — minor watch on stable intent given Micky Hammond's recent 3/13 form; monitor market moves in the final hour as any significant support would warrant attention in a wide-open bottom-of-the-handicap contest.

races.name: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears 3yo with placed form at 5f Good, but a natural hold-up horse; carrying 130lbs and forced into midfield by sheer weight of closers in this field, meaning it races against its grain throughout.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty 3yo whose best recent effort was a third at 5f Good, but sim-going record is thin and she arrives as a genuine closer who will struggle to get her preferred rearward berth with so many others seeking the same position.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran with a win from 15 Good-ground starts and clear course-and-distance experience, but the deeper closer role this race forces on him is not what his form pattern demands and the weight of years makes improvement on recent finishes hard to project.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; six-year-old with two wins and five places from nine 5f Good runs, wears a tongue-tie, and Hope Regan (7lb claimer) gets the chance to simply dictate — Declan Carroll sends out one winner from eight over 14 days which is fair context for a front-runner's chance.

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: Mark Walford 3yo returning from 18 days off who has placed twice on Good turf at 6f — stepping down to 5f today and, ridden by Olivia Haines, looks the most plausible horse to press Irish Dancer into a genuine contest if given a positive ride.

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster 3yo with a poor sim-going record of 0 wins and 2 places from 12 Good-ground efforts; consistent at finishing mid-to-rear and trainer has sent out 0 winners from 10 runners over 14 days, offering little angle to upgrade.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Michael Dods 5yo who has placed three times in his last five 5f Good runs and is the natural beneficiary if Irish Dancer's controlled pace is pegged back in the final furlong; wears a tongue-tie, carries 138lbs top weight, and Shay Farmer will need to position forward quickly to avoid being swallowed by the pack.

runners_data.name: Sunlit Sea
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott 3yo who won last time out over 5f Good and has a headgear change (blinkers) to sharpen focus; genuinely enters as one of the live threats, though her natural hold-up style, redistributed here to midfield, means the shape does not organically suit her best running.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby 8yo carrying the crossnoseband, with three placed efforts from nine 5f Good runs — solid recent form including a second and third — but as a true closer shuffled into midfield by the field composition, he needs the pace to collapse late for his effort to land.

races.paceDynamic: Irish Dancer is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the gates, she should be allowed to dictate a controlled, even gallop on Good ground over this sharp Thirsk 5f. That uncontested lead on a flat, fair-weather surface creates a race run at a steady-to-honest clip rather than a searingly fast early pace, which typically rewards horses who can travel prominently and pounce in the final furlong rather than those arriving late from off the pace. The overwhelming majority of the remaining eight runners — including Albegone, Sunlit Sea, Dabbling, Gwen Tennyson and So Grateful — are natural hold-up types, and with so many closers crowding the rear the race shape strongly favours those who can position close to Irish Dancer early and utilise the moderate pace. The field carries more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back, and those most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch are Midnight Lir and Mare Of London, who have the profiles and connections to be ridden positively off this single pace-setter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Irish Dancer Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Irish Dancer is allowed to stride into a clear lead from stall one and sets an honest but uncontested pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Irish Dancer controls every yard of the race, the pace is sustainable rather than punishing, and the most danger comes from horses travelling just off her shoulder rather than from deep closers arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Fight Out Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Lir and Mare Of London press Irish Dancer hard from halfway, injecting a late dash into the race.
scenarios.body: The tempo lifts in the back two furlongs, turning the race into a driving finish between the three horses closest to the pace, with fitness and weight-carrying ability becoming decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly entering the final furlong and the closers find a gap to burst through.
scenarios.body: Albegone or Sunlit Sea, both with recent placed form on Good ground at 5f, deliver a late run through a tiring field, though this scenario relies on them finding room from a congested rear group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If a bunched midfield group causes interference that frees one hold-up runner on a clear passage down the far rail.
scenarios.body: A horse like Dabbling or Gwen Tennyson, forced wide to get a clear sight, benefits from late shuffling among the pack, though their redistributed position makes this a low-probability outcome dependent on traffic more than merit.

watchPoints.text: Irish Dancer's early lead is the fulcrum of the entire race — watch whether Hope Regan establishes a clear margin within the first furlong or is immediately harried, as this determines whether the pace becomes a true test or a dawdle.

Midnight Lir carries top weight of 138lbs and must be ridden prominently by Shay Farmer to avoid being squeezed out in a field of nine closers — if he gets buried in the pack his placed form at 5f Good becomes academic.

Albegone and Sunlit Sea are genuine form horses but both are natural hold-up types competing for the same ground at the rear; monitor the draw and early positioning, as traffic trouble between them is a real possibility.

Mare Of London steps down from 6f to 5f for the first time and arrives 18 days fresh — how quickly Olivia Haines gets her into a prominent position off the first bend will reveal whether the trainer has targeted this shape deliberately.

Country Artiste's trainer Craig Lidster has recorded 0 winners from 10 runners in the past 14 days, and the horse's sim-going figures (0W from 8 Good runs) make it a difficult proposition to build a case around regardless of scenario.
